source.publication: Goldman Sachs Research (via Yahoo Finance) / JPMorgan (via GuruFocus, MarketBeat)

description: Two Tier-1 banks revised cybersecurity sector models upward in the same 30-day window, meeting the CLAUDE.md registration bar (>=2 of {GS,JPM,MS,BofA,UBS}, >=10% target change). Goldman Sachs (analyst Gabriela Borges, 2026-07-21) raised 12-month price targets on CrowdStrike ($182->$208, +14.3%) and Palo Alto Networks ($330->$371, +12.4%), both Buy-rated, explicitly reframing the sector: 'the Security category has shifted from being viewed as at risk from AI to being a clear beneficiary' as AI spend increasingly flows into security budgets. JPMorgan (analyst Brian Essex, 2026-06-30) separately upgraded Qualys to Neutral from Underweight, price target $87->$139 (+59.8%), citing vulnerability-management growth tied to the same AI-driven demand dynamic; JPM raised the QLYS target again to $150 by 2026-07-27. This is a live exit-timing signal for the open cybersecurity_commercial position (USPY.L) -- the 'security is a loser to AI agents' mispricing that partly motivated the original entry thesis is closing as consensus catches up.
user_notes: Registered 2026-07-28 scheduled scan (Pass 2). Position-relevant: cybersecurity_commercial is an open real-book holding (USPY.L, mov_20260608_cybersecurity_commercial_diversifier_experiment). Flagged in the review's analyst-model-revision table as a signal the sector's AI-beneficiary re-rating is broadening beyond CrowdStrike/Palo Alto (mega-caps) into mid-cap vulnerability management (Qualys) -- narrative maturity likely moving from 'emerging' toward 'mainstream', which cuts against future upside (crowding penalty) even as it validates the original thesis. Re-check narrative_maturity in the next sector study refresh.
